chunks: And as for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abu al-Jarud that he heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

saying: 'In al-ilan (oath of abstinence from conjugal relations), he is stopped after one year.' I said: 'After one year?' He said: 'Yes, he is stopped after one year.' This is not contradictory to what we have previously established that the duration of stopping is four months, because he said 'he is stopped after one year' and did not mention that if it is less than that, he is not stopped, and the speech indicates that, and we turn away from the indication of the speech with another indication, and we have previously established what necessitates turning away from its apparent meaning.

key_terms.الْإِيلَاءِ: Oath of abstinence from conjugal relations

ai.seo_question: What is the duration of the waiting period for al-ilan according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the one-year waiting period for *al-ilan* is clarified not as a contradiction to the four-month period, but as a distinct legal phase where the husband is 'stopped' from consummating the marriage. Shaykh al-Tusi uses this to demonstrate the Shia principle of *al-inkisaf 'an al-zahir* (turning away from the apparent meaning) when supported by other evidence, resolving the tension between the literal text and the established jurisprudential ruling.
